function: Joint learned control of RIS phase shifts, V2V power and channel choice, minimizing V2I age of information and raising V2V payload success (p. 3, 5)
system: Uplink V2I: single-antenna vehicles, BS with M=4 element ULA, K=4 V2V pairs; passive reflecting RIS with F=12 elements, 8 phase levels; 2 GHz, 1 MHz (p. 3, 8)
method: Soft Actor-Critic deep reinforcement learning, single central agent; fully connected actor and two critics (three hidden layers of 512), Adam, 1000 training episodes (p. 7-8)
data_channel: Python vehicular simulator built per 3GPP TR 36.885 and WINNER II (path loss, shadowing, Rayleigh fading); 450x650 m road grid; RIS links own model (p. 4, 8)
test_conditions: Trained 1000 episodes; tested 10 rounds of 50 slots, sweeping V2I power, V2V payload, RIS elements (10-120) and users (4-12); retraining per setting not stated (p. 8-11)
baselines: Learned: PPO, TD3, DDPG on the same problem; non-learned: random RIS with random resource allocation, and no RIS with random resource allocation (p. 9)
metrics: Reward, V2I age of information, V2I sum rate, V2V payload transmission success probability, versus V2I power, payload size, number of RIS elements and users (p. 9-11)
complexity: Training-stage order O((E*S-I)(GE+GA+2GC+UE+UA+4UC)) in abstract gradient and update costs; no inference cost or runtime (p. 8)
q1_support: p. 8: "We construct the vehicular environment according to [58], [59] and [60]". The references are 3GPP TS 22.186, 3GPP TR 36.885 and WINNER II (p. 13); Table I (p. 8) lists WINNER+ B1 Manhattan path loss, shadowing and Rayleigh fading; the RIS links use the paper's own model (p. 4).
q2_support: p. 8: "At the end of the training, we conduct tests based on the training model". Not met: the paper never says the trained policy is applied to a setting not used in training; the sweeps of V2I power, payload, RIS elements and users (p. 9-11) do not state whether the policy is retrained.
q3_support: p. 9: "In this group we will use three different algorithms, PPO, TD3, and DDPG" (learned); "Random RIS Random RA" sets the RIS phase shifts and the resource allocation at random (non-learned). Compared on V2V success rate, V2I rate and AoI (Figs. 5-8), e.g. "improved by 33.2%".
q4_support: p. 8: "the complexity of our approach in the training stage is O ((E · S − I)(GE + GA + 2GC + UE + UA + 4UC ))". Met as an order of complexity of the training stage, in abstract gradient and update costs; no inference complexity, FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 3: "The source code has been released at: https://github.com/qiongwu86/RISRB-AoI-V2X-DRL.git"
notes: Preprint arXiv 2406.11245v2 of the TVT paper. Included: the SAC agent chooses the RIS phase shifts and V2V power jointly with the spectrum-channel allocation, so it passes the above-PHY check as a joint decision (p. 5); area 3 for the RIS configuration. The objective is the age of information, not a classical PHY metric. q1 flagged for the reviewer: the channel is a custom Python simulator that the paper says follows 3GPP TR 36.885 and WINNER II (another standardized model, not TR 38.901), and the RIS cascaded links use the paper's own model (eq. 5, p. 4). q2: not stated whether the policy is retrained for each sweep; F and M change the state and action size. q4: the only complexity result is the training-stage O(.) in abstract symbols.
